#Vault: a native client for Bitwarden accounts

Status: phases 0 and 1 are written, phases 2 and 3 for the most part (see Implementation state). The rest is the plan. The protocol between Wren and the helper is in vault-protocol.md.

The feature gives Wren a built-in password manager client for Bitwarden® accounts. It is optional and off by default. It needs no WebExtension. The interface name of the feature is Vault. "Bitwarden" appears only as the name of the compatible service (see Trademark).

The main design decision comes from the license of the SDK (section 2.3): the SDK cannot be linked into wren.exe. It runs in a separate program, wren-vault, under GPL-3.0. The separate program is also the stronger security design (section 3).

#1. Scope

#1.1 User flows

FlowWhat the user doesPhase
EnableSets vault.enabled in the settings. Wren installs the helper and shows the Vault toolbar button.1
Log inTypes the email and the master password. Types a TOTP code if the account asks for one.1
UnlockTypes the master password in the unlock dialog.1
Fill from the panelOpens the Vault panel, sees the logins for the current site, selects one. Wren fills the form.1
Server choiceSelects US, EU, or a self-hosted server URL before the login.2
Other login methodsEmail 2FA code, new-device verification code, personal API key.2
Unlock on startWren starts locked with the account remembered. The user unlocks with the master password or a PIN.2
LockWren locks after an idle time, on system sleep, on demand, and at exit.2
SyncWren syncs after unlock, on a timer, and on demand.2
Fill from a keyPresses the fill shortcut. Wren fills the only match, or opens the list of matches.3
Fill from a fieldFocuses a login field. A dropdown anchored to the field lists the matches.3
Fill from the address barA chip in the address bar shows the number of matches. A click opens the list.3
Vault searchTypes the Vault prefix in the command palette. Selects an item to fill it, copy a value, or open its site.3
Per-site listThe panel lists every login of the current site, with copy actions for user name, password and TOTP code.3
TOTPCopies the current code, or fills a one-time-code field. The clipboard is cleared after a delay.3
Save or updateAfter a form submit, Wren asks to save a new login or to update a changed password.4
GeneratorIn a new-password field, the dropdown offers a generated password.4
PasskeysThe vault is an authenticator for navigator.credentials.create() and get().5

#1.2 Non-goals for phases 1 to 5

  • Login with SSO, trusted devices, Key Connector, or "log in with device".
  • 2FA with WebAuthn, Duo, or YubiKey OTP. Workaround: log in with a personal API key (phase 2).
  • Unlock with biometrics, and "never lock".
  • Cards, identities, secure notes, SSH keys: no fill, no edit. The search lists logins only.
  • Attachments, Send, import, export, emergency access, account registration, master password change.
  • Organization administration, collection management, policies that change the interface.
  • Several accounts at the same time. One account per profile.
  • URI match type "regular expression". Such a URI matches nothing until a later phase.
  • Automatic fill on page load. Wren fills only after a user action (section 3.5).
  • macOS.

#2. The SDK

#2.1 Which repository

RepositoryContentUse
bitwarden/sdk-internalThe Password Manager SDK that the official clients use: crypto, login, sync, vault, TOTP, generators, passkeys.This one.
bitwarden/sdk-sm (the older bitwarden/sdk; crate bitwarden 2.1.0 on crates.io)The public Secrets Manager SDK. It has no vault of logins.Not applicable.

State of sdk-internal on 2026-11-12: commit 300aea5, workspace version 4.0.0, tag rust-v4.0.0 (b865d1db), minimum Rust 1.89.0, edition 2024. Wren's toolchain (1.99.1) is sufficient.

#2.2 Stability

  • The README says: "The password manager interface is unstable and will change without warning."
  • Each crate says: "This crate does not follow semantic versioning."
  • Bitwarden gives no support for third-party use.
  • crates.io has only a part of the crates (bitwarden-core, bitwarden-crypto, bitwarden-auth, bitwarden-state, bitwarden-generators at 4.0.0). bitwarden-pm, bitwarden-vault 4.x, bitwarden-sync, bitwarden-unlock and bitwarden-fido are not published.

Consequences:

  • Depend on the Git repository, with one exact rev for all crates. Start with tag rust-v4.0.0 if it contains bitwarden-pm, bitwarden-sync and bitwarden-unlock. If not, use commit 300aea5.
  • An SDK update is a planned task with its own test run. It is never automatic.
  • All SDK calls stay in one Rust module of the helper (vault/src/sdk.rs). The protocol to Wren does not show SDK types.
  • The server API changes with time. An old pinned SDK can fail against a new server. Plan one SDK update per quarter.

#2.3 License verdict

Every crate we need declares GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Bitwarden-SDK. We must select one of the two. Wren's code is under PolyForm Strict 1.0.0, and Wren is distributed to third parties and sells licenses.

Bitwarden SDK License Agreement v2 (7 October 2025): blocking.

  • Section 3.1 permits only: (a) to develop, test and demonstrate a Compatible Application; (b) personal use by your family; (c) internal business operations with a paid Bitwarden server license.
  • Section 3.1 ends: "in no case above may the Compatible Application be offered, licensed, or sold to a third party."
  • Section 3.4 forbids redistribution of the SDK or any part of it.
  • Section 1.3 requires the application to work with the official server products.

A distributed browser, free or paid, is not permitted under this license.

GPL-3.0-only, linked into wren.exe: blocking.

A static link makes one combined work. The whole work must then be under GPL-3.0. PolyForm Strict is not compatible with GPL-3.0. Wren does not change its license for this feature.

GPL-3.0-only, in a separate program: compatible, with conditions.

The helper wren-vault is a separate program under GPL-3.0-only. Wren starts it and talks to it through pipes. The conditions are:

  1. The helper has its own source directory with its own LICENSE (GPL-3.0-only). Its source is public, complete, and includes the build instructions and the pinned SDK revision.
  2. The helper is not a part of wren.exe. It is a separate file with its own license notice. about:licenses names it.
  3. The protocol between Wren and the helper is documented and generic: requests and answers about accounts and logins. It does not pass SDK data structures. The helper has no dependency on Wren.
  4. No Wren code under PolyForm Strict is copied into the helper. Code that the two share (none is planned) must be licensed for both by its author.
  5. Each release of the helper keeps its matching source available (a tagged commit).
  6. The copyright and license notices of the SDK stay intact.

Residual risk: the FSF position is that two programs that talk through pipes are normally separate works, unless the communication is "intimate". Condition 3 addresses this. This document is not legal advice. The safest path is a written confirmation from Bitwarden Inc. (see section 6).

The GPL option has two benefits. We can patch the SDK when needed (section 2.5). We can test against Vaultwarden, which the SDK License does not permit.

#Trademark

The Bitwarden Trademark Guidelines apply whatever the code license is.

  • Do not use the Bitwarden logo. The toolbar icon is Wren's own (a vault or a shield).
  • Do not put "Bitwarden" in a product, feature, file or domain name. The feature is "Vault". The helper is wren-vault.
  • Refer to the service as an adjective, with the mark on first mention: "Use a Bitwarden® account".
  • Do not suggest endorsement. The settings page says that the feature is not made or supported by Bitwarden Inc.

#2.4 Crates and API surface

The helper depends on bitwarden-pm (the PasswordManagerClient that groups the sub-clients). Features: default only. Do not enable wasm, uniffi, bitwarden-license, no-memory-hardening, dangerous-crypto-debug or debug-capabilities. The directory bitwarden_license/ (commercial code) is never compiled.

NeedSDK callState in the SDK

The SDK repository contains crates/bw, a test CLI in Rust. It is the reference for a native consumer.

#2.5 Build

The request was a crate wren_vault in native/, behind a C ABI. The license forbids this. The design is:

  • A new top-level directory vault/: one Cargo workspace, one crate wren-vault (a binary), its own Cargo.lock, its own LICENSE (GPL-3.0-only) and README.md. It is not a member of native/.
  • wrentool build vault runs cargo build --locked with the release or quick profile, as wrentool build native does. The output is build/vault/wren-vault (.exe on Windows). build.bat and build.sh do not build it by default: the browser builds and runs without it.
  • All versions are exact. The SDK and passkey-rs are Git dependencies with an exact rev. The Nix flake vendors them with importCargoLock and outputHashes.
  • wrentool gen rust-crates writes a second list for the helper. about:licenses shows it under its own heading.
  • Patches to the SDK, if needed (device type, new-device code), are files in vault/patches/, applied to the vendored source by wrentool build vault. Keep the number of patches small. Offer each patch upstream.

Reasons other than the license to keep the SDK out of wren.exe:

  • bitwarden-crypto installs a #[global_allocator] (a zeroizing allocator). In wren_native it would replace the allocator of all Rust code of the browser: decoders, network, WebGL.
  • Wren writes minidumps on a crash. A vault in the process would put keys in the dump.
  • rusqlite with bundled SQLite adds a C build to wren_native.

Cost. These are estimates. Phase 0 measures them and writes the numbers here.

ItemEstimate
Crates in the helper's lock file350 to 450 (the full SDK workspace has 734, with WASM, UniFFI and CLI code)
Clean build, release2 to 4 minutes
Helper size, stripped6 to 12 MB
wren.exe size and build timeNo change
Helper startLess than 50 ms

#2.6 Async runtime

The helper runs one tokio runtime (rt-multi-thread, 2 worker threads). One task reads requests from stdin. One task writes answers to stdout. Each request runs as its own task. Wren's process gets no new runtime.

#2.7 Network

The SDK makes its own HTTP calls with reqwest 0.13, rustls (ring) and rustls-platform-verifier.

TopicSDK client in the helper (selected)Wren's stack (src/net, src/fetch)
WorkNone.Replace the transport under about 60 generated API calls, through IPC. Not practical.
TLS rootsThe system trust store. The same policy as wren_net.Same.
network.tls.extra_ca_fileNot applied. A private CA must be in the system store.Applied.
Proxyreqwest reads the proxy environment variables. Phase 0 checks the system proxy on Windows.System proxy.
Cookies, cache, blocker, DevToolsNot involved. Vault traffic is invisible to pages and to DevTools. This is intended.Would need exclusions.
HTTP/3No.Yes. Not needed here.

Rules:

  • The helper connects only to the configured server: the identity URL and the API URL. It follows no other URL. Icons of sites are not fetched in the first phases.
  • https is mandatory. http is accepted only for a loopback host (127.0.0.1, [::1], localhost). The tests use it.
  • The user agent is Wren/<version> wren-vault/<version>. The device identifier is a random UUID made at the first login and kept in the helper's state. The device name is "Wren".

#3. Security model

#3.1 Where secrets live

DataLocation
Master key, user key, organization keys, private keyHelper memory only. Never sent on the pipe.
Decrypted items (names, user names, URIs, passwords, TOTP seeds, passkey private keys)Helper memory only, decrypted on demand.
Access token, refresh tokenHelper memory. At rest: see 3.4.
Master password, PIN, 2FA codeTyped in Wren's dialog. Sent once on the pipe. Wren zeroes its buffer after the send.
Rows on screen (item id, name, user name, matched host, flags)Wren memory, only while the panel, dropdown or palette that shows them is open. Zeroed on close.
One password, one TOTP codeCrosses the pipe only at a fill or a copy that the user asked for.

The helper inherits the SDK's protections: zeroize on key types, the zeroizing global allocator, keys pinned on the heap. Do not disable them.

The helper adds:

  • No core dump: PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 and RLIMIT_CORE=0 on Linux; no Windows Error Reporting dump on Windows.
  • No debugger attach from a process of the same user on Linux (the same PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0).
  • It exits when stdin closes. A dead Wren leaves no unlocked helper.
  • It writes no secret to stderr. The SDK's tracing output is off in release builds.

#3.2 Lock is process exit

Locked means: no helper process holds keys. To lock, Wren sends lock. The helper drops the SDK client and exits. The operating system then frees every page. Wren starts a new helper at the next unlock.

This removes one class of defects: no code path has to find and clear each copy of a key.

Lock triggers: the toolbar or palette command, the idle timer (vault.lock.idle_minutes), system sleep or session lock, the exit of the last window, a disabled vault.enabled. The helper has its own idle deadline as a second guard: Wren sends a keepalive on user activity; without one, the helper locks itself.

#3.3 What crosses the boundary

The boundary is one pair of anonymous pipes (stdin, stdout) that the helper inherits. No socket and no named pipe exist: no other process can connect.

Frames are a 4-byte length and a JSON object. Maximum frame: 1 MiB. Each request has an id; each answer repeats it.

RequestCarries to the helperCarries to Wren
helloProtocol version, state directory, server URLs, device nameHelper version, account state (none, locked) and email
loginEmail, master password, optional 2FA or new-device codeok, or need_two_factor with the providers, or need_device_code, or an error
login_api_keyClient id, client secret, master passwordok or an error
unlockMaster password or PINok or an error with the tries left
lock, logoutNothingok
syncNothingCounts and the last sync time
logins_forPage URL, host, registrable domain (from Wren's Public Suffix List)Rows: id, name, user name, matched host, match type, has TOTP, has passkey
searchQuery text, offset, limit, kindsRows as above, and the count of all matches
fillItem id, the wanted fields (username, password, totp)The values
totpItem idCode and seconds left
save_login, update_passwordSite URL, user name, password, optional item idNew item id
generateOptionsOne password
pin_set, pin_clearPINok
passkey_* (phase 5)The authenticator requestThe authenticator response
keepaliveNothingNothing

Events from the helper: state (locked, unlocked, syncing, logged out), sync_done, error.

Rules in Wren for these values:

  • Never log a frame, a row, or a value. The package src/vault has no log call that takes payload data.
  • Crash reports hold no vault data: Wren holds rows only while a surface is open, and passwords only during a fill.
  • Remote control (wren ctl), CDP and BiDi have no vault method. They cannot read rows, trigger a fill, or unlock. Captures draw the Vault surfaces as an empty box. Only vault.test.remote (default off) lifts this, for e2e tests with a throwaway profile and a test account.
  • DevTools shows no vault traffic and no vault state.
  • The accessibility tree exposes rows as the screen shows them. It never exposes a masked value.
  • A page's scripts cannot reach src/vault: no api/*.widl function exists for it. This is rule 6 of architecture.md: the guest cannot reach host memory.
  • Session restore, history, bfcache snapshots and form restoration never store a value that the vault filled.

#3.4 State on disk

Directory: <profile>/vault/ (mode 0700). With browser.profile.persist off, the helper uses the SDK's memory database and nothing is written.

FileContentProtection
state.sqlite (SDK-managed)Items, folders, organization data: encrypted by the server-side scheme with the user key. Account email, server URLs, KDF parameters, device identifier. The PIN envelope when a PIN is set.File mode 0600. Useless without the master password or the PIN.
TokensAccess and refresh tokens.Phase 1: in state.sqlite. Phase 2: the helper implements ClientManagedTokens over the system store.

System store for tokens (phase 2), with the Rust crate keyring:

  • Windows: Credential Manager (DPAPI, bound to the user account).
  • Linux: Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) when a service answers. If none answers, a file of mode 0600. This is the same level as Chromium without a keyring, and as src/wasm/crypto_unix.odin.

A stolen token alone gives only encrypted data. The user key is never stored, except inside the PIN envelope. A PIN is weaker than the master password: the helper counts wrong PINs in its state and deletes the envelope after 5.

Phase 0 must list exactly what the SDK writes to state.sqlite at the pinned revision, and update this table.

logout deletes the directory content and the system store entry.

#3.5 Phishing resistance of fill

Definitions: the frame origin is the origin of the document that contains the field. The top origin is the origin of the tab's top document.

  1. A fill needs a user action. Wren never fills on page load. The action is a click on a row, the fill shortcut, or a selection in the dropdown. The action must come from the user's input device, not from a script or remote control.
  2. Matching uses the frame origin, never the page title, the form action, or the top origin.

  3. Match rules follow the item's URI match type:

    • Domain (the default): the registrable domain of the URI host equals the registrable domain of the frame host. Wren's Public Suffix List decides (src/url/psl.odin). A host with no registrable domain (an IP address, localhost, a public suffix) uses the Host rule.
    • Host: host and port are equal.
    • StartsWith: the frame URL starts with the URI.
    • Exact: the frame URL equals the URI.
    • Never: no match.
    • RegularExpression: no match (non-goal).
    • The account's equivalent domains (GlobalDomains) extend Domain from phase 3.
  4. One list decides. The helper selects candidates with the registrable domain that Wren sends. Wren checks each returned row again with its own list before it shows the row. The two sides use one Public Suffix List.
  5. Scheme. An item saved for https does not match an http frame. On an http frame (not loopback), Wren shows a warning with the origin and needs a confirmation for each fill. vault.fill.insecure can set this to never.
  6. Certificate errors. No fill on a page that the user opened through a certificate warning.

  7. Frames.

    • Same origin as the top document: fill.
    • Cross-origin frame: rows are for the frame origin. The list shows the frame origin in a warning line. Each fill needs a confirmation.
    • Opaque origin (sandboxed frame, data:, about:blank without an inherited origin): no fill.
  8. Fields. Wren fills only fields that are visible, enabled and editable, and that belong to the same form (or the same form-less group) as the field the user acted on. A password goes only into type=password fields.
  9. No fill into a field whose frame changed between the request and the answer. The fill carries the page's handle and navigation id. A dead handle drops the fill (rule 2 of architecture.md).
  10. Search results from the palette fill only when the item matches the current frame by the rules above. For a non-matching item, the palette offers "open the site" and "copy", not "fill".

A filled value is in the page. Its scripts can read it. This is the nature of every password manager. Rules 1 to 10 limit which page gets it.

#3.6 Clipboard

A copied password or TOTP code is removed from the clipboard after vault.clipboard.clear_seconds (default 30), if the clipboard still holds that value. On Windows, the copy is marked to stay out of the clipboard history.

#3.7 Helper integrity

Wren runs the helper only from a path that it controls, and only when its SHA-256 equals the value built into this Wren version. vault.helper.path (for development and for packagers) overrides the path; a policy file can forbid it.

#4. Integration design

#4.1 Distribution of the helper

wren.exe has no file beside it. This rule stays. When the user enables the feature:

  1. Wren shows what will happen: a download of wren-vault (size, license GPL-3.0, link to the source).
  2. Wren downloads the helper of its own version from the release assets, with the code of gui_toolkit update.
  3. Wren checks the SHA-256 that is built into wren.exe, then stores the file in <data dir>/vault/<version>/.
  4. A Wren update downloads the matching helper before the first unlock. Old versions are deleted.

Linux packages (Nix, others) install wren-vault beside wren. Wren finds it there and downloads nothing.

#4.2 Packages

PackageRole
vault/ (Rust, GPL)The helper: protocol, SDK calls, state, token store.
src/vault (Odin)The client: protocol codec, process start and stop, the state machine, the match check, settings. No UI. No dependency on browser or page.
src/forms/credentials.odinFinds login fields in a document (4.6).
src/browser/vault_*.odinThe shell: toolbar button, dialogs, panel, dropdown, prompts, palette source, settings section.
src/webauthn/platform_vault.odinThe vault as a WebAuthn Platform (phase 5).

#4.3 State machine

One explicit state per App, in src/vault. Every surface reads it. No surface keeps its own copy.

Disabled -> Helper_Missing -> Installing -> Logged_Out -> Logging_In -> (Need_Two_Factor | Need_Device_Code) -> Unlocked
                                            Locked -> Unlocking -> Unlocked -> (Syncing) -> Unlocked
Unlocked -> Locked            (lock, idle, sleep)
any -> Failed(reason)         (helper exit, protocol error); the next user action starts again from Locked or Logged_Out

Logged_Out or Locked at start comes from a small file that Wren owns (<profile>/vault/account: email and server URLs only). Wren does not start the helper to draw the locked icon.

A second machine exists per fill: Requested -> Answered -> Applied | Dropped. A request has a deadline (vault.request.timeout_ms). A late answer is dropped and zeroed.

#4.4 Threads

  • The vault state belongs to the App and changes only on the loop thread (rule 3 of architecture.md).
  • One reader thread per helper process blocks on the pipe. It only decodes a frame and calls host.post.
  • Writes to the pipe go through the blocking pool, in order. The loop thread never blocks on the helper.
  • Thread memory starts from base.process_context(). Frame buffers come from a base.Arena per frame, zeroed on free.
  • With browser.shell.page_thread, the loop hands a fill to the page's thread as it hands input events.
  • Two Apps in one process (the e2e two_apps test) have two helpers and two state machines. No global is added.

#4.6 Forms

What src/forms has today: control kinds, Input_Type (with Password, Email, Tel, Text), values with the user_edited flag, form ownership, submission (submit.odin). It has no reading of the autocomplete attribute and no login detection.

New, in src/forms/credentials.odin, as pure functions over the DOM and the forms model:

  • autocomplete_tokens(node): parses the attribute by the HTML rules (section prefix, username, current-password, new-password, one-time-code, email, webauthn).
  • login_fields(document, anchor): returns the group of the anchor field: user name, current password, new password (and its confirmation), one-time code. The group is the field's form, or the nearest common ancestor for fields with no form.
  • Order of evidence: autocomplete tokens; then type=password; then for the user name the nearest text, email or tel field before the password; then name, id and inputmode hints for one-time codes (otp, totp, 2fa, 6 digits).
  • A multi-step login (user name page, then password page) gives a group with one field. It is valid.

The fill writes through the forms model as a user edit: it sets user_edited, and dispatches input and change as typing does. Frameworks then see the value.

The save offer (phase 4) hooks the submission path in src/forms/submit.odin through the Host (submitting); 4.10 says how. The card and address fields are in src/forms/autofill.odin (4.10).

#4.7 Shell surfaces

All are toolkit widgets drawn by the chrome. None is a web page. None lives in a page's DOM, so a page cannot read, cover or style them.

  • Toolbar button: one icon with three states (logged out, locked, unlocked) and a count of matches for the tab. Hidden when vault.enabled is off.
  • Login dialog and unlock dialog: modal for the window, like confirm_shell. The password field is a toolkit secure field: masked, no copy, zeroed on close. The dialog shows the account email and the server host.
  • Panel: anchored to the toolbar button. Lists the matches for the active tab, then a search field. Row actions: fill, copy user name, copy password, copy TOTP code, open the site. Footer: sync, lock, settings.
  • Field dropdown: anchored to the focused login field with the geometry that forms_shell records while painting (Painted). Drawn in the overlay pass, as the select list is. Keyboard: Down opens, Enter fills, Escape closes. When locked, it shows one row: "Unlock the vault".
  • Address bar chip: shown when the active tab has matches. A click opens the panel.
  • Palette source: a Palette_Source with its own prefix. It asks the helper for rows when the palette opens in that mode, and releases them on close. Commands: lock, unlock, sync, open the panel, generate a password.
  • Save and update offer: under the toolbar's Vault button (4.10). It never steals focus. Actions: save, update, never for this site, not now.
  • Settings section: account (email, server, log out), lock, fill, save, clipboard, the license and source link of the helper, the "not made by Bitwarden Inc." line. If generic parts emerge (secure text field, anchored list), they go into gui_toolkit.
  • Strings go through i18n.

#4.8 Passkeys (phase 5)

Wren's src/webauthn keeps the client work: options, RP ID check, clientDataJSON, timeouts, extensions. platform_vault.odin implements the Platform interface. make_credential and get_assertion send the authenticator request to the helper, which runs bitwarden-fido's Fido2Authenticator. The helper implements Fido2CredentialStore over the vault, and Fido2UserInterface as protocol events that Wren answers with its own prompt (pick a credential, confirm the creation, unlock first).

The page's conditions do not change (secure context, user activation, focused tab, one ceremony at a time).

Selection between authenticators: when the vault is enabled, a chooser lists "Vault" and "This device or a security key". For get() with an allow list, the helper answers first whether it holds one of the credentials (silently_discover_credentials). If it holds none, Wren goes directly to the system authenticator. Conditional mediation (autocomplete="webauthn") then becomes possible through the field dropdown.

#4.9 WebExtensions

docs/extensions.md does not exist yet. The Vault does not depend on it and uses none of its mechanisms.

If the user also installs the Bitwarden extension:

  • The two run side by side. They share no state and no session. Each has its own login and its own lock.
  • A login field then shows two dropdowns: Wren's and the extension's inline menu. Wren does not hide either.
  • An extension that replaces navigator.credentials in the page takes the passkey call before Wren's code.
  • Wren detects the extension by its identifier and shows one line in the Vault settings: use one of the two. It disables nothing by itself.
  • Wren does not provide the native-messaging host of the Bitwarden desktop application.

#4.10 Saving, the generator, the code after a login, cards and identities

Protocol 5 (save, generate, the kinds of items, the fields of cards and identities: vault-protocol.md).

  • Save offer (vault.save.offer). forms.Host.submitting runs inside a submission, after its validation and before its submit event (whose listeners may empty the fields), and for form.submit() too. The page hands it to the shell (page.Forms_Embedder.submitting), which reads the form's user name and password (forms.sent_login: a filled new-password field first) and gives them to vault_offer_capture. The Vault compares them with the site's rows: a document's set that is ready for that address, else for another address of the same host (the page after a login). When none is ready yet (the Vault was unlocked a moment before, the rows are on their way), the offer waits for them (Waiting) at most 10 s (OFFER_WAIT_MS), then is dropped. No login with this user name (case does not matter): Save. One: its password is asked of the helper (a fill whose answer goes to no hook), then Update if it differs, nothing if it is the same. The offer's state machine: None, [Waiting], [Checking], Save or Update, Saving, None.
  • A login sent by a script (no form submission: a click handler reads the fields and posts them with fetch). forms.Forms.typed_password is the password field the person last typed into (set_edit_text: only the person's edits, never a script's value or a fill). A form submission that owns it clears it (typed_sent): the submission's offer had it. The page asks forms.unsent_login once, when the document goes (page_unload, page_freeze for the back/forward cache, forms_detach for a closed tab; before pagehide, whose listeners may empty the field) or when the field leaves the document (the DOM's removal hook; looked at again at the next task, so that a form a script only moves is not taken). It gives a login when the field still holds a value that the person typed (a script's value over it gives nothing) and is a password field; the user name is the group's (its form, or the fields with no form, in the field's own tree: a removed form still holds its fields): autocomplete username or email, else the nearest text field before the password. The page hands it to the shell (page.Forms_Embedder.login_left), which captures it as a form's login: the offer shows over the tab's next page.
  • The offer hangs under the toolbar's Vault button: the host, the user name, Save or Update, Not now, Never for this site. It is not modal and takes no focus. Save creates a login named after the host with the page's address; Update changes the password (and adds the address when no URI of the login matches it). The rows are asked again after the answer. "Never for this site" keeps the host in <profile>/vault/never_save (one host a line, written by a blocking job, one write at a time); no offer is made there again.
  • The captured password is a secret: it is zeroed when it crossed to the helper, at a dismissal, at another capture and at a lock.
  • Generator (vault.generator.*). Under a password field that takes a new password (autocomplete new-password, or two password fields in its form) or of a site with no login yet, the dropdown ends with "Generate a password": the helper generates it, and it fills every new password field of the form (the password and its confirmation). The shell keeps the value for that form until it is sent, for the save offer. The panel's "Generator…" opens a dialog: password or passphrase, its length or its words, its classes; the value is made again at each change, with Regenerate and Copy (the clipboard is cleared after vault.clipboard.clear_seconds).
  • The code after a login (vault.totp.autofill). After a fill of a login that has a code, when its form had no code field, the shell waits 2 minutes for a one-time-code field (forms.one_time_code_field) in the focused document of the same site (the same registrable domain), and fills the code there once. The document is looked at again only when its tree or its attributes change. Never in a frame of another origin or on a plain http page. vault.totp.copy_on_fill copies the code right after the login's fill.
  • Panel search: the field at the top of the unlocked panel. Empty: the page's logins. Typed: the whole vault (search), every kind, "N items" (the helper's total) under the field, each row with the icon of its kind and its acts: a login fills (when it is one of the page's) and copies its user name, password and code; a card copies its number and security code; an identity its email. The list is the toolkit's lazy column (ui.lazy_begin): only the rows near the view are built. The helper answers one page of 100 rows (SEARCH_PAGE); when the rows built come within half a page of the last row held, the next page is asked (vault_search_more) and appended, one page at a time, until total. A page of an older query (another gen of the set) or of another offset is dropped; a page that fails ends the paging of that query and keeps its rows.
  • Cards and identities (src/forms/autofill.odin). autofill_role gives a field's role from its autocomplete (cc-name, cc-number, cc-exp, cc-exp-month, cc-exp-year, cc-csc, cc-type; name, given-name, additional-name, family-name, honorific-prefix, email, tel, organization, street-address, address-line1 to 3, address-level1 and 2, postal-code, country, country-name), else from the words of its name and id (cardnumber, cvv, expmonth, firstname, zip, city...). A login's role wins over it. The dropdown under such a field lists the vault's cards or identities (an empty search with kinds ["card"] or ["identity"], kept in its own set, Items, while such a field has the focus; more than 6 rows scroll in a lazy column, which asks the next page as it nears the end); a pick fills every field of that kind in the form: an expiry date as MM/YY or MM/YYYY by the field's placeholder and maxlength, a select by its option's value or text. Social security, passport and licence numbers are never asked.

#5. Phases

Each phase ends with something the user can try. Each phase adds to a product that works.

#Test strategy (decided)

LevelWhatWhen it runs
Odin unit testssrc/vault and src/forms/credentials.odin against a fake helper: an in-process implementation of the transport that answers from a table. Covers the codec, the state machine, deadlines, match rules, zeroing.Always (test_all).
Rust testsThe helper against wiremock on loopback (the SDK's own test dependency): prelogin, token, 2FA, sync, errors. Fixtures are made once from a test account.wrentool test vault (cargo test --locked), in CI.
e2eWren headless + the real helper + Vaultwarden on loopback, with a seeded account. Scenarios in src/tools/e2e/vault_*.odin.Opt-in (-Vault). CI on Linux only; the flake provides vaultwarden.
ManualOne login, sync and fill against bitwarden.com (US and EU) with a real account.Before each release that changes the helper or the SDK revision.

No automated test contacts bitwarden.com. Tests wait for a state with a bound, never for a fixed delay.

#Phase 0: foundation

  • Record the license decision of section 6.
  • vault/ with LICENSE, the pinned SDK, hello and the frame codec. wrentool build vault, wrentool test vault.
  • Flake: vendored Git dependencies, a check that builds the helper, hooks for the new Rust and TOML files.
  • Measure and write in 2.5: crate count, build time, size. Write in 3.4 what the SDK persists. Check the proxy behaviour and the device type value that the server accepts.
  • Try: wrentool vault probe --server http://127.0.0.1:<port> logs in to a local Vaultwarden and prints the item count.

#Phase 1: enable, log in, unlock, list, fill

  • src/vault: settings, process start, codec, state machine, fake helper. Requests: hello, login (email, master password, TOTP 2FA), unlock, lock, sync (once after unlock), logins_for, fill.
  • Helper: Domain and Host matching; state in state.sqlite; US server by default, vault.server.url for tests.
  • src/forms/credentials.odin: user name and password fields.
  • Shell: the preference in the settings, the install step, the toolbar button, the login and unlock dialogs, the panel with the matches of the active tab, fill of the top frame.
  • Tests: unit (state machine, match rules with PSL cases such as github.io, IP hosts, ports, scheme); Rust (login with and without TOTP, wrong password, sync); e2e (enable, log in, fill a form of examples/site, check that wren ctl cannot read rows).
  • Try: enable the Vault, log in with TOTP, open a login page, fill it from the panel. Restart Wren, unlock, fill again.

#Phase 2: session life

  • Server region (US, EU, self-hosted). Email 2FA, new-device code, API key login, logout.
  • PIN unlock, idle lock, lock on sleep, helper self-lock, periodic sync, sync command.
  • Tokens in the system store (ClientManagedTokens).
  • Tests: PIN try counter, lock triggers with an injected clock, token store fallback on Linux without Secret Service.
  • Try: use a self-hosted or EU account; leave Wren idle and see it lock; unlock with a PIN.

#Phase 3: fill everywhere

  • Fill shortcut, field dropdown, address bar chip, palette source, per-site list, copy actions with clipboard clearing.
  • TOTP copy and fill of one-time-code fields. Frames (rule 7). StartsWith, Exact, Never, equivalent domains.
  • Tests: dropdown geometry under transforms and scroll, frame rules, palette rows released on close.
  • Try: focus a login field and fill from the dropdown with the keyboard only.

#Phase 4: write to the vault

  • Save and update prompt, "never for this site", generator in new-password fields, folders in the save prompt.
  • Tests: submit detection for form posts and script logins, no prompt in private windows, conflict when the item changed on the server.
  • Try: create an account on a site with a generated password; accept the save prompt; see the item on another device.

#Phase 5: passkeys

  • platform_vault.odin, the chooser, passkey_* requests, conditional mediation.
  • Tests: the WebAuthn vectors of src/webauthn against the vault platform; e2e registration and login on a local relying party of src/testserver.
  • Try: register a passkey on a site into the vault, then sign in with it.

#Later

2FA with WebAuthn, Duo and YubiKey; SSO; biometrics unlock; regular expression URIs; site icons.

#6. Risks and open questions

#Risks

  • SDK instability. The API changes without notice. Mitigation: one pinned revision, one module that calls it.
  • Server drift. A new server can refuse an old client. Mitigation: a quarterly SDK update; an error that tells the user to update Wren.
  • License change. Bitwarden can change the license of future SDK versions (it did so in 2024 and 2025). The pinned GPL revision stays usable. A fallback exists: implement the protocol without the SDK, as rbw does.
  • Legal reading of "separate program". See 2.3. Not tested in court for this case.
  • Client identity. The SDK login sends device type ChromeBrowser. The server shows the device to the user and can apply rules per client type. Phase 0 selects a truthful value and patches the SDK if needed.
  • Account risk. Bitwarden's terms for its hosted service apply to the user. A third-party client is not forbidden today (rbw and others exist), but Bitwarden gives no guarantee.
  • Supply chain. The helper adds some hundreds of crates and two Git dependencies. All are pinned by hash.

#Decisions taken (2026-11-12)

  1. License: the GPL-3.0 helper as a separate program.
  2. Source: a separate repository, wren-vault (locally ../wren-vault), not a vault/ directory of Wren. It holds no Wren code. It must be public before the first release that offers the Vault.
  3. Delivery: download on enable. Phase 1 locates the helper only (see "Implementation state").
  4. Naming: "Vault", with "Use a Bitwarden® account" in the settings.
  5. Test server: Vaultwarden on loopback, Linux CI only (not written yet).
  6. Private CA: the system store.

#Decisions for you (as first written)

  1. License path. Accept the GPL-3.0 helper as a separate program (recommended), or ask Bitwarden Inc. first for a written permission or a commercial agreement. A permission would also allow a static link, but the separate process stays the better security design.
  2. Source location of the helper. A directory vault/ in the Wren repository with its own GPL license (recommended: one build, one version), or a separate public repository. If the Wren repository is private, the helper source must be public elsewhere.
  3. Delivery. Download on enable (recommended: wren.exe stays one file), or ship the helper in the installer.
  4. Naming. "Vault" with "Use a Bitwarden® account" in the settings (recommended), or another name. A name that contains "Bitwarden" needs a written permission.
  5. Test server. Vaultwarden on loopback for opt-in e2e tests, Linux CI only (recommended). The alternative is the official self-hosted server in a container, which is heavier. A dedicated test account on bitwarden.com is needed for the manual checks: who creates and owns it.
  6. Private CA for self-hosted servers. Accept "install the CA in the system store" (recommended), or patch the SDK client to read network.tls.extra_ca_file.

#Implementation state

Phases 0 and 1, and phases 2 and 3 for the most part, as written on 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13. Where the code differs from the plan above, this section is the truth.

#The helper (wren-vault, a separate repository)

  • SDK: bitwarden/sdk-internal at 300aea5933ef3bc139e430575b6868b9a9b1d4a7 (workspace 4.0.0). The helper depends on the crates it calls (bitwarden-core with internal, bitwarden-auth, bitwarden-vault, bitwarden-sync, bitwarden-crypto-sync-handler, bitwarden-api-api, bitwarden-crypto), not on bitwarden-pm: fewer crates to build, and the same calls. All SDK calls are in src/sdk.rs.
  • Login: the helper sends its own token request (src/identity.rs), not the SDK's login_password, which sends device type ChromeBrowser, one device identifier for every SDK user, and no new-device code (2.4). No SDK patch is needed. The SDK still does the prelogin, the master password hash (MasterPasswordAuthenticationData::derive), the sync, the keys (initialize_user_crypto with the sync's unlock data), the PIN and the items. The request names client id web, device type 14 (UnknownBrowser, also the SDK client's Device-Type), the device name Wren and the account's own random device identifier. A renewal with an API key goes through the SDK and names its fixed device.
  • Second steps: the authenticator code (provider 0) and the email code (provider 1; the helper asks the server to mail it with the SDK's send_two_factor_email, and the server mails it by itself when it is the account's only second step); the new-device code as newDeviceOtp, sent from the same device identifier as the first step. Duo, WebAuthn and YubiKey: unsupported_two_factor, and the personal API key logs in (client_credentials).
  • Sync: the SDK's SyncClient with a sync handler of the helper that keeps the encrypted items, the master password unlock data, the account keys, the organization keys and the account's email (an API key login learns it there).
  • Unlock after a restart: initialize_user_crypto with MasterPasswordUnlock and the kept unlock data, or with PinEnvelope and the kept PIN envelope. The refresh token (or the API key) and the login method go back into the client's state with an expired empty access token; the SDK's token handler renews it at the first request.
  • PIN: crypto().enroll_pin; the envelope and a try counter are in state.json; the fifth wrong PIN in a row deletes the envelope. Not with browser.profile.persist off (the helper refuses: no_state).
  • Tokens (3.4): not ClientManagedTokens. The SDK's own token handler keeps the tokens in the client's memory; the helper writes the refresh token and an API key's client secret to the system store after each login and sync when they changed (src/tokens.rs): keyring-core with dbus-secret-service-keyring-store (libdbus, synchronous, on tokio's blocking threads) on Linux and windows-native-keyring-store on Windows; else tokens.json (mode 0600). The access token is never stored. Only a short text goes to the store: the Credential Manager takes at most 2560 bytes, less than an access token.
  • State: state.json version 2 (mode 0600, directory 0700), not the SDK's SQLite database: the SDK's own persistence is moving between revisions, and one file of encrypted values is easier to audit. The helper's README lists its fields. A version 1 state is not read: the account logs in again.
  • Requests run one after the other, in the order they come (not a task each): the answers keep the order of the requests, and a hello sent with a login is always handled first. The loop waits on the next frame and on the idle deadline at once (FrameReader is cancel safe); at the deadline it writes the event locked and exits.
  • Protocol 3 (helper 0.3.0, phase 3): search (each word of the query in the name, the user name or a URI; sorted by name; at most 50 rows; no password); totp and fill with totp (the SDK's generate_totp: otpauth, steam and base32 keys); logins_for applies StartsWith and Exact (the URL standard's serializations) and the equivalent domains. The sync asks for the domains (excludeDomains=false) and keeps the groups (the account's own, then the global ones it did not exclude) in state.json (equivalent_domains).
  • Not yet: the successful-login fixtures of the wiremock tests (they need a test account), the measures of 2.5, the list of what the SDK writes (3.4: the SDK writes nothing; the helper writes state.json and tokens.json or the system store's entry).

#Wren

  • src/vault: the state machine (Disabled, Locating, Helper_Missing, Logged_Out, Logging_In, Need_Two_Factor, Need_Device_Code, Locked, Unlocking, Unlocked, Failed), the fill's own machine (Requested, Answered, Applied, Dropped), the codec, the transport, the match check, the settings. Tests run it against a fake helper, the timers on a virtual clock.
  • Servers: vault.server.region (us, eu, self) and vault.server.url. The account file (<profile>/vault/account) holds the email, the server's identity address and the PIN mark; an account of another server is not remembered. A private CA: the system store (decision 6), said in the preference and in the dialog.
  • Timers of an unlocked Vault, on the loop: the idle lock (vault.lock.idle_minutes; input of the browser window postpones it, main.odin calls vault_shell_activity with each frame's events) and the sync (vault.sync.interval_minutes). Activity sends a keepalive at most once a minute; the helper's own deadline is the Vault's and 120 s. A change of vault.lock.idle_minutes while unlocked moves Wren's timer at once and the helper's deadline at the next unlock.
  • Threads: writes go through a writer thread per helper, not the blocking pool: one thread keeps the order, and the pool's workers do not wait on a pipe. The blocking pool locates the helper, reads and writes the account file (one job at a time: a logout's removal is never undone by an older write), checks the rows and joins an ended helper's threads.
  • Shell (src/browser/vault_shell.odin): the toolbar button (in the toolbar row; not yet in the sidebar's title bar), its panel (rows, Sync, Lock, Set a PIN / Remove the PIN, Log out), the login dialog (server, email and password or API key, then the authenticator or email code, or the new-device code), the unlock dialog (master password or PIN), the PIN dialog, the question before a fill on plain http, the fill of the top document.
  • Remote control: while it is on (unless vault.test.remote), the panel is an empty box, the tooltip is not shown, and the dialogs close and zero their fields: a capture of the window shows nothing of the Vault.
  • Forms (src/forms/credentials.odin): autocomplete_tokens, login_fields, fill_field. A filled field is marked (Control.vault_filled, until a reset or a script's value): history restoration (page/history_state.odin) skips it, and a document with a filled field is not kept in the back/forward cache (Forms.vault_filled). Session files hold no form values at all. The fill clears the field's undo steps.
  • The helper is found, not downloaded: vault.helper.path, else wren-vault beside the browser, else in its vault folder (build/vault/ beside build/wren). The download on enable (4.1), with the SHA-256 built into Wren (3.7), needs release assets of the helper: a later step.
  • Automation: wrentool build vault, wrentool vault test, wrentool vault probe (it asks for a second step's code on its input).

  • Phase 3 (src/browser/vault_fill.odin):

    • The target of a fill is the document that holds the focused field: the focused frame's, else the tab's. The Vault keeps four sets of rows (Row_Slot): the tab's document (Page), the focused frame's document (Frame), the search of the palette or the panel (Search), the cards or the identities while a card or address field has the focus (Items). Search and Items hold their search page by page. This changes 3.1: the rows of the tab's document stay in Wren's memory while the Vault is unlocked, not only while a surface shows them: the chip, the fill shortcut and the dropdown need them without a round trip to the helper. They are zeroed at a lock, at another address, and when remote control starts. Search rows go when the palette closes. No password and no code is ever in a row.
    • Fill shortcut: the command vault.fill (Ctrl+Shift+L, vault.fill.shortcut; guarded: the key is the page's while the Vault is off). Locked: the unlock or login dialog. Unlocked: the only row at once; several: the dropdown on a login field, else the panel. Other commands: vault.search, vault.unlock, vault.lock, vault.sync, vault.panel.
    • Dropdown: toolkit boxes over the page (vault_dropdown_build, after the palette), at the field's painted bounds (forms_control_screen_rect: the bounds of the transformed box, so a rotated or scrolled field anchors where it shows); under the field, above it without room. hud_captures keeps presses on it from the page. Keys (vault_dropdown_key, before the page's keydown, while it shows): Down and Up move (Up past the first row gives the keys back to the field), Enter fills the chosen row (no row chosen: Enter is the page's), Escape hides it on this field until Down. The field's role (forms.login_role: user name, password, one-time code) is computed again only when the focus, the document's tree or its attributes change. On a one-time-code field it lists the logins with a code and fills the code. Locked: one row, "Unlock the Vault".
    • Chip (vault_chip, in address_chips): the number of the tab's logins (a click opens the panel); locked, on a login field, "Vault locked" (a click opens the unlock dialog).
    • Palette: the source "Vault", prefix $, not in the plain search. items asks the helper (vault_search, once per query: the helper searches, off the interface thread) and lists, per login, its acts: "Fill" (only when the item is a checked row of the focused document: rule 10), copy the user name, the password or the code, open the site. The palette lists the first page (100 rows) and its own fuzzy match runs on those.
    • Per-site list: the panel's rows have Copy user name, Copy password and Copy code. A copy is a fill (or totp) request whose answer goes to the copy hook, never to a page. The clipboard is cleared after vault.clipboard.clear_seconds if it still holds the value: Wren keeps only its hash and length.
    • TOTP: a fill writes the code into the group's one-time-code field (Login_Fields.one_time_code: autocomplete one-time-code, or a name or id with otp, totp, 2fa, mfa..., or a numeric field named code of 4 to 8 characters) when the row has a code.
    • Frames (rule 7): frame_fill_rule. The frame's own origin and address decide its rows. Same origin as the top document: fill. Another origin: the dropdown names it, and each fill asks first (the question names the frame's host; a yes fills only the document it was asked for: same tab, same frame or not, same forms model). Opaque origin: no rows, no fill. about:blank and srcdoc frames have no web address: no fill, even with an inherited origin. The fill's ticket names the document (page, its forms model's id, the field): a frame that went or navigated drops the fill.
    • Not yet: rule 6 (no fill after a certificate warning: the browser has no such bypass state to read yet); the Windows clipboard history exclusion (3.6: the toolkit's clipboard has no such flag; a gui_toolkit change); the dropdown in a frame whose fields the shell paints in another document's pass (Forms_View.painted holds one document at a time: the dropdown then does not show, the shortcut and the panel still fill); the e2e scenarios of phase 3.
  • Phase 4 and cards (src/browser/vault_save.odin, src/forms/autofill.odin, protocol 5): see 4.10. Not yet: folders in the offer, a conflict when the item changed on the server.
  • Not yet: lock on system sleep and session lock (vault.lock.on_sleep: the toolkit reports no such event yet); the fill on the page thread when browser.shell.page_thread is on (the fill runs on the loop thread, as the chrome's focus moves do); the e2e tests against Vaultwarden; about:licenses listing the helper; the flake's check of the helper.
